rides_nothing: Mars's wind moves the dust: the drift blows over the ground round the camp and the devils wander the plain on their own; nothing of the camp carries them

about: What Mars's wind does to its dust round the camp, as the game 2099 draws it (MarsWind, DustDevil, #116): on the calm afternoon the scene record holds, the drift's fine grains blowing along the ground on the five by five cells round the camp's middle and two dust devils wandering the plain in sight of the outside cameras; in a dust storm (the variant `storm`) the drift thick, fast and head high and no devils. The drift moves here, so the scene record's still drift (Sky/Dust) is made inactive in this layer. The devils are now measured on real footage (the footage block: Spirit's Gusev films and Greeley's counts): each one see-through column of fine dust about 10 m across at its foot, not the game's 1.2 m speckled columns, the east one stood where its downwind wandering keeps clear of the domes; the drift keeps the game's numbers, its height checked on the footage, and no grain of it blows inside the domes (`interiors`). Real footage checked before: the Spirit rover's Gusev crater films of dust devils (NASA/JPL, 2005: slim see-through columns, narrow at the foot, widening as they climb) and the Apollo 16 film for fine dust reading as a veil (2099's #116, the owner's rule that many fine grains read and big sparse ones do not).

footage.how: Read off the papers' text and measured on the rovers' frames' pixels against the size their captions give. Measured on the bake 5 s into the stage's time (the looped devils and drift stand whole all the time): the devil from where its foot stands then, the drift over the planned ground beneath it.

doi-10.1029/2006JE002743.what: Greeley et al. 2006, active dust devils in Gusev crater, Mars, seen by the Spirit rover (JGR 111, E12S09), 533 devils
doi-10.1029/2006JE002743.measured: read (its abstract): 2 to 276 m across, most 10 to 20 m; moving 1 to 21 m/s; the wind up the column 0.2 to 8.8 m/s; at least 95 m and up to at least 848 m high

lpi-7thmars2007-3149.what: Greeley et al., Spirit's second dust devil season (7th International Conference on Mars, abstract 3149)
lpi-7thmars2007-3149.measured: read: 23.7 m across on the mean (16 devils), moving about 4.5 m/s on the mean

PIA07253.what: Spirit's navigation camera, sol 486, a dust devil about 1 km away, 34 m across and moving 4.8 m/s (NASA/JPL, 21 frames)
PIA07253.measured: measured on the frame's pixels against the caption's 34 m: the foot about 38 px across, about 52 px across 60 m higher (about 6 degrees either side); a thicker lower column about 2.4 foot widths high, a fainter one past the frame's top at 4.2 foot widths and more; leaning about 5 degrees downwind; the ridge behind shows through the column, no single grains

PIA07925.what: Spirit's navigation camera, sol 446, a dust devil passing close below the rover (NASA/JPL)
PIA07925.measured: looked at: the lowest part flares like a funnel, 20 to 30 degrees either side; the ground's streaks show through the whole column, no single grains

doi-10.1088/0034-4885/75/10/106901.what: Kok, Parteli, Michaels and Karam 2012, the physics of wind-blown sand and dust (Reports on Progress in Physics 75)
doi-10.1088/0034-4885/75/10/106901.measured: read (its table 3, Mars): sand hopping along the ground about 10 cm high and about 1 m long at twice the threshold, almost ten times higher and longer than on Earth

doi-10.1029/2005JE002491.what: Greeley et al. 2006, wind-related features in Gusev crater (JGR 111)
doi-10.1029/2005JE002491.measured: read: grains up to about 300 micrometres blown onto the rover's deck in gusts; devils lean downwind
